drills.name: Middle Tee Contact Baseline
drills.purpose: Establish a contact baseline at a comfortable middle location.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Tee at a comfortable middle-height, middle-of-plate location slightly in front of the plate. Broad center-field target on the net.
steps: Hit 4–6 balls at controlled effort toward the center target.
Build to normal game intent on the last 2.
drills.cue: Square it up, then add speed.
drills.mistake: Chasing distance and losing balance on every swing.
drills.correction: Score solid contact first; add intent only when contact stays solid.
drills.progression: Alternate with H04/H05 heights; move to H22.
drills.success: 4 of 6 solid contacts toward the broad target.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Inside Tee Contact Point
drills.purpose: Deliver the barrel to an inside pitch with contact farther out front.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Tee on the inner half, set farther forward than the away setup. Pull-side gap target.
steps: Confirm the contact point is out front.
Take 4–6 swings toward the pull-side gap.
Check that contact is on the barrel, not the handle.
drills.mistake: Tee set too deep, so the hitter gets jammed and learns to push the hands away.
drills.correction: Move the tee forward until barrel contact is comfortable.
drills.progression: H08 Inside-Outside Tee Switch; H23 Inside-Lane Front Toss.
drills.success: Barrel contact on most swings; ball travels toward the pull-side gap.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Outside Tee Opposite-Field Drive
drills.purpose: Cover the outer half without reaching or diving.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Tee on the outer half at a deeper contact point. Opposite-field gap target.
steps: Take 4–6 swings toward the opposite-field gap.
Keep the landing controlled; no step across the plate.
drills.cue: Let it travel; drive through it.
drills.mistake: Stepping across the plate or reaching with the arms to get to the ball.
drills.correction: Use a flat landing marker (H15) and move the tee slightly closer.
drills.success: Firm opposite-gap contact with a consistent landing.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Top-of-Zone Tee
drills.purpose: Adjust posture and bat path to a higher pitch; reduce an unnecessary dip-and-lift.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Tee near the top of the hitter's strike zone (not above it), 4–8 inches in front of the plate.
steps: Hit 5 balls at controlled effort aiming for line drives.
drills.mistake: Coaching it as 'swing down' or chopping at every pitch.
drills.correction: Ask for firm line drives, not ground balls; keep the normal swing shape.
drills.success: Line drives without a large dip-and-lift; contact holds when the tee returns to middle.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Bottom-of-Zone Tee
drills.purpose: Adjust to lower strikes without collapsing or reaching.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Tee near the bottom of the hitter's strike zone, slightly in front of the plate.
steps: Rehearse matching the low height with the legs and posture.
Hit 4–6 balls toward a broad line-drive target.
drills.cue: Get to the low pitch, then turn.
drills.mistake: Dropping the back shoulder to scoop, or bending only at the waist.
drills.correction: Lower the target height expectation; use H06 to contrast heights.
drills.success: Firm contact without falling off balance.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Low-Middle-High Tee Sequence
drills.purpose: Adjust barrel delivery to pitch height at a consistent plate location.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: One tee moved through low, middle, and high heights at the same plate location.
steps: Low → middle → high, one swing each.
Then use a changing order the hitter doesn't choose.
drills.mistake: Using the identical swing for every height.
drills.correction: Pause between heights and name the height before each swing.
drills.success: Solid contact at all three heights in at least one ladder.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Full Strike-Zone Tee Map
drills.purpose: Explore contact across three heights and three plate locations.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Tape a 3×3 grid on the plate area or use markers; move the tee through the nine zones.
steps: One swing per zone in a set order.
drills.cue: Each zone has its own contact point.
drills.mistake: Leaving the tee at the same depth for inside and outside.
drills.correction: Inside farther forward; outside deeper.
drills.success: Identifies weak zones; solid contact improves on the repeat swings.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Inside-Outside Tee Switch
drills.purpose: Change contact depth while keeping the landing consistent.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage; flat landing marker
drills.setup: Two tees (or one moved) set inside/forward and away/deeper. Landing marker on the ground.
steps: Seek pull-gap contact inside and opposite-gap contact away.
drills.mistake: Changing the stride direction to reach each location.
drills.correction: Return to H15 landing-spot work, then retry.
drills.success: Consistent landing on at least 5 of 6 swings.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Coach-Called Location Tee
drills.purpose: Connect pitch location with an appropriate contact plan.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Coach repositions the tee before the hitter sets up. Broad pull, middle, and opposite targets.
steps: Coach sets inside, middle, or away.
Hitter names the intended broad target.
drills.cue: Match the contact to the location.
drills.mistake: Forcing every pitch opposite field, or slicing weakly and calling it success.
drills.correction: Score solid contact and direction separately.
drills.success: Solid contact + intended direction on 4 of 6.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Reduced-Ball Tee Precision
drills.purpose: Make centered contact the task.
drills.equipment: Bat, helmet, compatible tee, suitable smaller practice balls, net
drills.setup: Tee sized for the smaller ball at a comfortable middle location.
drills.mistake: Slowing the swing to guide the bat.
drills.correction: Keep normal intent; accept misses as information.
drills.success: Centered contact on at least half the swings without slowing down.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Fixed-Base Tee Swings
drills.purpose: Simplify the swing and isolate rotation and contact.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Feet start near the hitter's normal landing width. Middle tee.
steps: Let the hips and shoulders turn naturally.
Finish with 2 normal-stride swings for comparison.
drills.mistake: Holding the front shoulder or knee closed on purpose.
drills.correction: Allow the back foot and hips to rotate; judge balance, not closedness.
drills.success: Balanced finish and solid contact; compare with normal swings.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Loaded-Hands Start Tee
drills.purpose: Examine barrel delivery after landing; separate stride problems from turn problems.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Stride foot already down; hands comfortably loaded near the rear shoulder.
steps: Compare with normal stride swings on video.
drills.mistake: Pushing both hands straight at the ball (casting) from the start.
drills.correction: Feel the body turn deliver the barrel; reduce effort first.
drills.success: If the dip or cast disappears here, the issue is in the load/stride; if not, it's in the first forward move.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Stride, Hold, Swing Tee
drills.purpose: Organize the landing and launch position; address hands that sink during the stride.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Middle tee. Video or mirror for feedback if available.
steps: Check hands in a comfortable launch position (not collapsed to the waist).
drills.mistake: Hiking the hands artificially high after landing.
drills.correction: Look for a comfortable, repeatable launch, not a fixed hand height.
drills.success: Hands arrive in a usable launch position on most reps.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Hold vs. Flow Tee Pairs
drills.purpose: Transfer a paused rehearsal back into a rhythmic swing.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Middle tee.
drills.mistake: Copying the pause into the game swing.
drills.correction: Keep the continuous swing fully rhythmic.
drills.success: Continuous swings keep the improvement seen in paused swings.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Marked Landing Tee
drills.purpose: Make front-foot landing direction repeatable (stepping out or diving).
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage; flat tape or chalk landing marker
drills.setup: Flat marker at the intended landing spot; leave room for a comfortable toe angle.
steps: Remove the marker for the last 2 swings.
drills.mistake: Looking down at the marker during the swing; locking the toe closed.
drills.correction: Glance before, eyes on ball during; judge location, not toe angle.
drills.success: Lands near the marker on 4 of 5; keeps it with the marker removed.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Lift-and-Hold Stride Tee
drills.purpose: Control the move into landing from rear-side support.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage; landing marker
drills.setup: Landing marker; middle tee.
steps: Lift the front foot slightly and hold briefly.
Place it at the marker without tipping.
drills.mistake: Long, stiff holds or collapsing the back knee.
drills.correction: Keep the hover short — control, not a balance test.
drills.success: Lands balanced and on target on most reps.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Short-Tap Stride Tee
drills.purpose: Reduce forward-move complexity (overstriding, lunging).
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Middle tee.
steps: Replace the stride with a small toe tap.
drills.mistake: Turning the tap into a big lift.
drills.correction: Keep the tap small and quiet.
drills.success: Balanced contact with less lunge.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Step-In Momentum Tee
drills.purpose: Explore rhythm and forward momentum into contact.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage; extra clear space behind the hitter
drills.setup: Middle tee; clear space for 2–3 walking steps.
steps: Controlled walk-in steps toward the plate area.
drills.mistake: Rushing the walk and losing balance.
drills.correction: Slow the steps; balance first.
drills.success: Controlled landing and solid contact.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Open-Stance Start Tee
drills.purpose: Explore barrel delivery from a moderately open starting orientation.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Hitter starts moderately open to the pitcher (comfortable, not extreme).
steps: Normal swings from the open setup.
Don't force a return to square.
drills.cue: Stay balanced and square it up.
drills.mistake: Treating the drill stance as a permanent change.
drills.correction: Always finish with normal-stance comparison swings.
drills.success: Balanced, solid contact; normal swings unaffected.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Closed-Stance Start Tee
drills.purpose: Explore rotation and contact from a moderately closed orientation.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted batting helmet, adjustable tee, practice balls, hitting net or cage
drills.setup: Hitter starts moderately closed; no strained hips, knees, or back.
steps: Normal swings from the closed setup.
drills.mistake: Over-closing until rotation is uncomfortable.
drills.correction: Reduce the offset immediately if anything strains.
drills.success: Comfortable rotation and solid contact.
drills.safety: Clear swing radius; no one stands near the hitter or in front of the net; helmet on; check tee stability.

drills.name: Side-Angle Toss Contact
drills.purpose: Introduce moving-ball contact.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: Feeder safely offset to the side, outside the swing and batted-ball paths; toss into the hitting zone.
steps: Track and make a normal two-handed swing.
drills.mistake: Rapid-fire tosses that rush the hitter.
drills.correction: Wait for the hitter's ready signal every time.
drills.success: Solid contact on 4 of 6.
drills.safety: Feeder behind a protective screen (front toss) or safely offset (side toss); hitter waits for a ready signal; helmet on; clear batted-ball path.

drills.name: Steady Middle Front Toss
drills.purpose: Establish rhythm and timing against a consistent moving ball.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: Feeder behind a protective screen 15–20 ft in front; consistent middle tosses.
steps: Same release and location every pitch.
drills.mistake: Inconsistent tosses becoming the main challenge.
drills.correction: Feeder practices location before the round.
drills.success: Solid contact on most tosses with the target movement intact.
drills.safety: Feeder behind a protective screen (front toss) or safely offset (side toss); hitter waits for a ready signal; helmet on; clear batted-ball path.

drills.name: Inside-Lane Front Toss
drills.purpose: Apply inside-pitch contact to a moving ball.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: Manageable inner-half tosses from behind the screen.
drills.mistake: Keeping the hands in so long that the ball reaches the handle.
drills.correction: Return to H02 and confirm the out-front contact point.
drills.success: Barrel contact on most inside tosses.
drills.safety: Feeder behind a protective screen (front toss) or safely offset (side toss); hitter waits for a ready signal; helmet on; clear batted-ball path.

drills.name: Outside-Lane Front Toss
drills.purpose: Cover the outer half without diving.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: Manageable outer-half tosses from behind the screen. Optional landing marker.
drills.cue: Let it travel; drive through it.
drills.mistake: Stepping across the plate to reach.
drills.correction: Add the H15 landing marker.
drills.success: Opposite-gap contact without diving on most tosses.
drills.safety: Feeder behind a protective screen (front toss) or safely offset (side toss); hitter waits for a ready signal; helmet on; clear batted-ball path.

drills.name: Up-Down Height Toss
drills.purpose: Adjust to pitch height with a moving ball.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: Manageable upper- and lower-zone tosses.
drills.mistake: Collapsing or reaching on every low pitch.
drills.correction: Return to H06 ladder.
drills.success: Solid contact on both heights.
drills.safety: Feeder behind a protective screen (front toss) or safely offset (side toss); hitter waits for a ready signal; helmet on; clear batted-ball path.

drills.name: In-Out Location Toss
drills.purpose: Adjust contact depth and direction to location.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: Two manageable locations.
steps: Alternate inside and away in a known order.
Then vary the sequence without announcing it.
drills.cue: Match the contact to the pitch.
drills.mistake: Guessing location and committing early.
drills.correction: Return to known order; track the ball longer.
drills.success: Appropriate direction and solid contact on most tosses.
drills.safety: Feeder behind a protective screen (front toss) or safely offset (side toss); hitter waits for a ready signal; helmet on; clear batted-ball path.

drills.name: Mixed-Location Read Toss
drills.purpose: Respond to location rather than memorize a pattern.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: High-in, high-away, low-in, low-away with moderate location differences.
steps: Score solid contact and intended direction separately.
drills.mistake: Feeder making the zones too extreme.
drills.correction: Keep all zones within the hitter's manageable range.
drills.success: Solid contact on at least half, with appropriate direction.
drills.safety: Feeder behind a protective screen (front toss) or safely offset (side toss); hitter waits for a ready signal; helmet on; clear batted-ball path.

drills.name: Change-of-Speed Toss
drills.purpose: Adjust timing without rushing.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: Two manageable toss speeds; visible delivery.
drills.cue: Wait for the ball, not the pattern.
drills.mistake: Lunging at the slower toss.
drills.correction: Smaller stride (H17) and a later start on the slow toss.
drills.success: On-time contact at both speeds.
drills.safety: Feeder behind a protective screen (front toss) or safely offset (side toss); hitter waits for a ready signal; helmet on; clear batted-ball path.

drills.name: Varied-Delivery Timing Toss
drills.purpose: Track the release instead of guessing when the pitch is coming.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: Consistent release area; feeder varies delivery rhythm slightly.
drills.cue: Move with the delivery; see the release.
drills.mistake: Turning it into a trick or quick-pitching the hitter.
drills.correction: Keep the release visible and fair.
drills.success: Stays on time on most tosses.
drills.safety: Feeder behind a protective screen (front toss) or safely offset (side toss); hitter waits for a ready signal; helmet on; clear batted-ball path.

drills.name: Open-Stance Front Toss
drills.purpose: Transfer an altered-position task to a moving ball.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: Comfortable open starting orientation; predictable tosses.
drills.cue: Stay balanced and square it up.
drills.mistake: Uncomfortable stance or treating it as a permanent setup.
drills.correction: Reduce the offset; always compare with normal swings.
drills.success: Solid contact in both setups.
drills.safety: Feeder behind a protective screen (front toss) or safely offset (side toss); hitter waits for a ready signal; helmet on; clear batted-ball path.

drills.name: Track Two, Attack the Third
drills.purpose: Observe ball flight before committing to a swing.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: Front toss or coach BP; three-pitch sequences.
steps: Attack pitch 3 if suitable; take it if clearly not.
drills.cue: Track two; attack a good third.
drills.mistake: Swinging at a bad third pitch because 'the drill says hit'.
drills.correction: Reward a correct take on pitch 3.
drills.success: Correct decision on every third pitch.
drills.safety: Pitcher behind an L-screen; follow league helmet and catcher-gear rules; control pitch counts for whoever throws; clear on-deck area.

drills.name: Single-Zone Hunt
drills.purpose: Practice a clear attack plan.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: Define a manageable attack area before the round.
steps: Swing at pitches in the area.
Take the rest, even some strikes.
drills.mistake: Abandoning the plan after one take.
drills.correction: Score decisions first; contact second.
drills.success: Follows the plan on at least 5 of 8 pitches.
drills.safety: Pitcher behind an L-screen; follow league helmet and catcher-gear rules; control pitch counts for whoever throws; clear on-deck area.

drills.name: Swing-or-Take Decisions
drills.purpose: Establish basic swing selection.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, practice balls, hitting net or cage, protective screen for the feeder (front toss) or safe offset position (side toss)
drills.setup: Mix clearly hittable pitches and clear balls.
drills.mistake: Judging the decision by the result.
drills.correction: Decision and outcome are scored separately.
drills.success: Correct decisions on most pitches.
drills.safety: Pitcher behind an L-screen; follow league helmet and catcher-gear rules; control pitch counts for whoever throws; clear on-deck area.

drills.name: Edge-of-Zone Reads
drills.purpose: Refine decisions on less obvious pitches.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, baseballs, L-screen for the pitcher, cage or field, catcher gear if a catcher is used, score sheet
drills.setup: Define the strike zone and task; present manageable pitches near one boundary at a time.
steps: Discuss uncertain calls without treating close decisions as failure.
drills.mistake: Inconsistent feeder location becoming the main challenge.
drills.correction: Use a skilled feeder or machine; mark 'unclear' when needed.
drills.success: Improves edge decisions across rounds.
drills.safety: Pitcher behind an L-screen; follow league helmet and catcher-gear rules; control pitch counts for whoever throws; clear on-deck area.

drills.name: First-Pitch Ready Round
drills.purpose: Practice prepared aggression without chasing.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, baseballs, L-screen for the pitcher, cage or field, catcher gear if a catcher is used, score sheet
drills.setup: Mini at-bats starting 0–0.
steps: Attack a pitch there; take an unsuitable pitch.
drills.cue: Ready to attack — not required to swing.
drills.mistake: Swinging at any first pitch.
drills.correction: Reward a good take as much as a good swing.
drills.success: Swings at attackable first pitches; takes poor ones.
drills.safety: Pitcher behind an L-screen; follow league helmet and catcher-gear rules; control pitch counts for whoever throws; clear on-deck area.

drills.name: Hitter's-Count Hunt
drills.purpose: Use a favorable count.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, baseballs, L-screen for the pitcher, cage or field, catcher gear if a catcher is used, score sheet
drills.setup: Start at 2–0 or 3–1.
drills.mistake: Expanding the zone in a hitter's count.
drills.correction: Narrow the attack area.
drills.easier: Front toss with a named zone.
drills.success: Swings mostly at pitches in the damage area.
drills.safety: Pitcher behind an L-screen; follow league helmet and catcher-gear rules; control pitch counts for whoever throws; clear on-deck area.

drills.name: Two-Strike Compete Round
drills.purpose: Compete with two strikes.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, baseballs, L-screen for the pitcher, cage or field, catcher gear if a catcher is used, score sheet
drills.setup: Start at 0–2, 1–2, or 2–2.
steps: Use appropriate competitive swings and takes.
drills.mistake: Rewarding swings at obvious balls as 'protecting'.
drills.correction: Protect the zone, not the whole box.
drills.success: Puts strikes in play or fouls them; takes obvious balls.
drills.safety: Pitcher behind an L-screen; follow league helmet and catcher-gear rules; control pitch counts for whoever throws; clear on-deck area.

drills.name: Move-the-Runner At-Bats
drills.purpose: Connect a hitting plan to a game situation.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, baseballs, L-screen for the pitcher, cage or field, catcher gear if a catcher is used, score sheet
drills.setup: Announce outs (fewer than two), runner on second, and team objective.
steps: Discuss which pitches support the task.
Play the sequence; don't force the same contact on every pitch.
drills.cue: Know the job; choose the pitch.
drills.mistake: Forcing an unsuitable pitch toward a predetermined field.
drills.correction: Choose the pitch first, then the job.
drills.easier: Front toss with the situation called.
drills.success: Good decision quality and appropriate execution.
drills.safety: Pitcher behind an L-screen; follow league helmet and catcher-gear rules; control pitch counts for whoever throws; clear on-deck area.

drills.name: Score-the-Runner At-Bats
drills.purpose: Execute a scoring approach.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, baseballs, L-screen for the pitcher, cage or field, catcher gear if a catcher is used, score sheet
drills.setup: Define outs, defensive alignment, and the intended task.
steps: Seek a pitch that can produce useful contact.
drills.cue: Find a pitch you can drive.
drills.mistake: Sacrificing all pitch selection to 'put something in play'.
drills.correction: Keep the attack area; adjust with two strikes only.
drills.success: Attacks drivable pitches; avoids weak chases.
drills.safety: Pitcher behind an L-screen; follow league helmet and catcher-gear rules; control pitch counts for whoever throws; clear on-deck area.

drills.name: Full-Count Live Battles
drills.purpose: Integrate recognition, decisions, timing, and contact.
drills.equipment: Bat, fitted helmet, baseballs, L-screen for the pitcher, cage or field, catcher gear if a catcher is used, score sheet
drills.setup: Complete at-bats from 0–0 with a score sheet.
steps: Track balls, strikes, takes, fouls, and outcomes.
drills.mistake: Coaching mechanics between every pitch.
drills.correction: Save feedback for after the at-bat.
drills.success: Decision and contact rates hold up against live pitching.
drills.safety: Pitcher behind an L-screen; follow league helmet and catcher-gear rules; control pitch counts for whoever throws; clear on-deck area.

rehearsals.name: No-Bat Landing Rehearsal
rehearsals.purpose: Find the intended landing without a swing.
rehearsals.how: Load and stride to the mark 3–5 times; freeze and check; no bat needed.

rehearsals.name: Lift-and-Balance Rehearsal
rehearsals.how: Small load; lift front foot slightly; brief hold; place at the mark balanced.

rehearsals.name: Hand-Position Freeze Check
rehearsals.purpose: Arrive in a usable launch position.
rehearsals.how: Load, stride, pause; check hands near the rear shoulder, not collapsed to the waist.

rehearsals.name: Band-Feedback Load Rehearsal (optional)
rehearsals.purpose: Feedback for the move into launch; NOT a resisted swing.
rehearsals.equipment: Very light band with handle, smooth stable anchor at loaded-hand height on the catcher side
rehearsals.how: Light tension; small load and stride; pause; slight hip opening without yanking the arms; return slowly; repeat unresisted.
rehearsals.cue: Feel the load; don't fight the band.

rehearsals.name: Guess-Then-Check Round
rehearsals.purpose: Connect feel with results in high-intent sessions.
rehearsals.how: 3–5 swings with one task; hitter predicts best swing; compare with contact, numbers, and video; change one thing or nothing; repeat.

rehearsals.name: Feel vs. Film Check
rehearsals.how: Record 3 swings; hitter labels each met/missed/unsure before viewing; review; count matches.
rehearsals.cue: Tell me what you felt, then let's check.

rehearsals.name: Rhythm Reset Round
rehearsals.purpose: Recover when a hitter is forcing intent.
rehearsals.how: End the round; check discomfort/fatigue; 2–3 rhythm swings; one short retest round; if quality is still worse, reduce difficulty or end high-intent work.
rehearsals.cue: Find the rhythm, then add speed.

flaws.whatYouSee: Front foot moves away from the plate before landing, or hip/shoulder pulls away during the turn.
flaws.checks: Mark landing spot; compare stride-only, stride-pause, and no-stride swings to see whether it starts before or after landing.
flaws.contributors: Stride direction habit; early pull of the front side; fear or difficulty with inside pitches; timing.
flaws.avoid: Locking the toe or knee closed; demanding 'stay closed' through contact.
flaws.progressMarker: More consistent landings on comparable swings.
flaws.retest: Score 10 swings on landing before and after (Video Log).

flaws.whatYouSee: Stride lands excessively toward the plate; reaching for away pitches.
flaws.checks: Check landing vs. intended line; check whether it happens only on away pitches.
flaws.contributors: Overcorrecting a bailout; trying to reach outer half; plate position.
flaws.avoid: Moving the hitter off the plate without checking contact depth first.
flaws.progressMarker: Landing stays on line on away pitches.

flaws.whatYouSee: Hands push outward early; arms extend before the barrel is delivered; wide barrel path.
flaws.checks: Pitcher-facing view: distance between hands and torso at swing start.
flaws.contributors: Sequencing; arms starting the swing; bat too heavy; reaching for outer pitches.
flaws.avoid: Hard barriers or rigid poles; telling the hitter to keep the arms bent forever.
flaws.progressMarker: Less early outward hand movement on video.
flaws.retest: Compare Loaded-Hands Start Tee swings with normal swings.

flaws.whatYouSee: Hands lower relative to the shoulder before or as the forward swing begins.
flaws.checks: Chest-facing view; compare starting hand height with landing; check whether delivery is affected.
flaws.contributors: Load pattern; timing; posture; hands starting too high for comfort.
flaws.avoid: Freezing the hands at one height; treating every lowering as a flaw.
flaws.retest: Hold vs. Flow Tee Pairs comparison.

flaws.whatYouSee: Hands or barrel dip then climb back to the ball; many popups or weak contact up in the zone.
flaws.checks: Check whether it's a hand dip or a barrel dip; check posture at landing.
flaws.contributors: Hand drop; posture; excessive attack angle for the pitch.
flaws.progressMarker: Firmer line drives on high-tee and high-toss.

flaws.whatYouSee: Front shoulder opens before the barrel is delivered; contact weak to the pull side or misses away.
flaws.checks: Check landing first (T01); check pitch location.
flaws.contributors: Bailout; guessing inside; trying to pull everything.
flaws.avoid: Holding the shoulder shut until after contact.
flaws.progressMarker: Firm opposite-gap contact on away pitches.

flaws.whatYouSee: Long stride; head and body drift forward; weak or early contact on off-speed.
flaws.checks: Measure stride length on video; compare toe-tap swings.
flaws.contributors: Trying to generate power with the stride; timing.
flaws.progressMarker: Shorter, repeatable stride with solid contact.
flaws.retest: Short-Tap Stride Tee vs. normal comparison.

flaws.whatYouSee: Weight stays over the back leg; hitter spins without moving into the front side.
flaws.checks: Chest-facing view of weight transfer at contact.
flaws.progressMarker: Balanced finish over a supported front side.
flaws.retest: Step-In Momentum Tee vs. normal comparison.

flaws.whatYouSee: Contact deep and on the handle; foul balls to the opposite side.
flaws.checks: Check start timing and contact point vs. pitch location.
flaws.contributors: Late start; long swing; inside-pitch contact depth.
flaws.avoid: Forcing faster hands without fixing start timing.

flaws.whatYouSee: Weak pull-side grounders; rolling over off-speed or away pitches.
flaws.checks: Check contact depth on away pitches; check stride timing.
flaws.contributors: Early commitment; guessing; contact too far forward away.
flaws.avoid: Telling the hitter to just 'wait' without a timing task.

flaws.whatYouSee: Soft contact or misses on the outer half.
flaws.contributors: Reaching; contact too far out front; diving.
flaws.cue: Let it travel; drive through it.
flaws.avoid: Moving the tee far away so the hitter must reach.

flaws.whatYouSee: Many high popups; ball contacted under center.
flaws.checks: Check pitch height vs. swing path; check posture.
flaws.contributors: Loop; dropping the back shoulder; attack angle too steep for the pitch.
flaws.progressMarker: More line drives from high and middle locations.

flaws.whatYouSee: Many hard or weak grounders; ball contacted over center.
flaws.checks: Check pitch height; check whether contact is early.
flaws.contributors: Contact too far forward; rolling over; posture.
flaws.avoid: Telling the hitter to uppercut everything.
flaws.progressMarker: More line drives on low and middle locations.

flaws.whatYouSee: Head or torso moves sharply during the swing; inconsistent contact.
flaws.checks: Video the head and torso from the chest view.
flaws.contributors: Overswinging; posture for pitch height; fatigue.
flaws.progressMarker: More centered contact with steady posture.

flaws.whatYouSee: Swings at pitches clearly out of the zone or attack area.
flaws.checks: Score swing/take decisions separately from contact.

flaws.whatYouSee: Takes pitches in the attack area; falls behind in counts.
flaws.checks: Score takes on good pitches; ask what the hitter was looking for.
flaws.contributors: Fear of failure; overthinking mechanics; unclear plan.
flaws.avoid: Adding more mechanical cues before at-bats.

flaws.whatYouSee: Good tee swings fall apart when the ball moves.
flaws.checks: Compare tee and toss video at the same checkpoint.
flaws.contributors: Timing; tracking; too big a jump in difficulty.
flaws.avoid: Rebuilding mechanics when the problem is timing.

flaws.whatYouSee: Effort rises but bat speed or contact repeatedly drops; rushing; old flaws return.
flaws.checks: Compare effort report with contact and any measured speed across rounds.
flaws.contributors: Fatigue; chasing numbers; too much volume.
flaws.cue: Find the rhythm, then add speed.

workflow.label: Observe
workflow.action: Film 5–10 comparable swings from the same angle; note one checkpoint.

workflow.label: Hypothesis
workflow.action: Pick the most likely cause using the Checks column.

workflow.label: Test
workflow.action: Run one recommended drill with one cue.

workflow.label: Retest
workflow.action: Film the same comparable swings; log in Video Log.

workflow.label: Decide
workflow.action: Keep, adjust, or step back one level. Don't stack corrections.

blocks.label: Tee
blocks.activity: Marked Landing Tee, then Fixed-Base Tee Swings

blocks.label: Transfer
blocks.activity: Steady Middle Front Toss, then Outside-Lane Front Toss

blocks.label: Tee
blocks.activity: Stride, Hold, Swing Tee → Hold vs. Flow Tee Pairs → Loaded-Hands Start Tee

blocks.label: Power block
blocks.activity: One selected drill, 2 × 3 per side (12 throws)

blocks.label: Toss
blocks.activity: Steady Middle Front Toss → Mixed-Location Read Toss with takes

blocks.label: Transfer
blocks.activity: Two 4-swing rounds of Steady Middle Front Toss

blocks.label: Timing
blocks.activity: Steady Middle Front Toss if available

blocks.label: Wednesday
blocks.focus: Don't add work to fill the day

blocks.label: Thursday
blocks.activity: S4 with M02 (or M06 if ready)

warmupRoutines.name: Standard Hitting Warm-Up
warmupRoutines.useFor: Before tee, toss, or batting practice
warmupRoutines.sequence: WU01 → WU02 → WU03 → WU04/WU05 → WU06 → WU08 → WU09 → WU11 (2 easy + 2 moderate) → WU12 (4–6 tee contacts) → WU13 if needed
warmupRoutines.note: Start easy; build gradually toward practice speed.

warmupRoutines.name: Youth Simplified Warm-Up
warmupRoutines.sequence: WU01 (game-style) → WU03 → WU05 → WU09 → WU11 (3 easy swings) → WU12 (3–4 tee contacts)
warmupRoutines.note: Familiar movements; short instructions; finish engaged, not tired.

warmupRoutines.name: Medicine-Ball-to-Hitting Prep
warmupRoutines.useFor: Sessions with a med-ball power block
warmupRoutines.sequence: WR1 general portion → WU14 rehearsal throws → planned med-ball block (Med Ball Library) → 1–2 min recovery → WU11 → WU12 → WU13
warmupRoutines.note: Throws before hitting only if the hitter stays coordinated.

warmupRoutines.name: Game-Day Routine
warmupRoutines.sequence: WU01 → WU02 → WU04 → WU06 → WU08 → WU09 → WU11 → WU12/WU13 if available
warmupRoutines.note: Familiar preparation only — no new drills, no med-ball records.

warmupRoutines.name: Between-Innings / Long-Wait Reset
warmupRoutines.useFor: Athlete already warmed up who has been sitting
warmupRoutines.sequence: WU03 (short) → WU08 → WU09 → WU11 (2–3 progressive swings, safe area)
warmupRoutines.note: Follow league rules for on-deck swings and timing.

warmupRoutines.name: Cold-Weather Adjustment
warmupRoutines.sequence: Extend WU01–WU02; repeat WU06–WU08; extra progressive dry swings before any contact
warmupRoutines.note: Layer clothing; extend gradually; don't rush to full intent.

warmupActivities.name: Knee Lifts / Skips
warmupActivities.how: Marching knee lifts progressing to easy skips.

warmupActivities.name: Lateral Weight Shifts
warmupActivities.how: Wide stance; shift weight hip to hip.

warmupActivities.name: Hip Hinges
warmupActivities.how: Push hips back with a long spine, then stand.

warmupActivities.name: Trunk Turns
warmupActivities.how: Controlled trunk rotations in a batting-width stance.

warmupActivities.name: Arm Circles & Wrist Prep
warmupActivities.how: Small-to-large arm circles; wrist circles and gentle flexion/extension.

warmupActivities.name: Band Pull-Aparts (optional)
warmupActivities.how: Light band pulled apart at chest height.

warmupActivities.name: Progressive Dry Swings
warmupActivities.how: Easy → moderate → normal effort swings with the game bat.

warmupActivities.name: Predictable Toss Progression
warmupActivities.how: Side or front toss at consistent middle location (H21/H22).

steps.action: Ask the coach for ONE current goal and ONE cue (use the Coach-Parent Plan sheet).
Check willingness: home practice is optional and short.
Check readiness: no pain, not exhausted, not right after a heavy game or pitching day.
Check the space with the Home Safety Checklist.
Pick one session from Sample Home Sessions (10–15 min).
Use the Parent Language guide: praise decisions and effort, not results.
Log the session in the Practice Log with Context = Home.
Stop for pain and tell the coach. Count games, lessons, and team practice before adding home work.

safety.check: Fitted batting helmet worn for all hitting
Clear swing radius — no people, pets, cars, or windows nearby
Net rated for baseballs and anchored
Tosser behind a protective screen (front toss) or safely offset (side toss)
Bat sized and league-legal for the player
Soft or practice balls in small spaces
Retrieve balls only when swinging has stopped
Dry footing; no practice in lightning or extreme heat

safety.why: Pain is not a coaching problem

sessions.sequence: Easy movement → 4 dry swings → H01 × 4 → H04 × 4 → 'What felt good?'
Easy movement → R01 × 5 → H15 × 5 → H01 × 4 (marker removed)
Easy movement → R03 × 4 → H13 × 4 → H14 × 4 pairs
Easy movement → H01 × 4 → H21 × 6 → H21 × 4 with a target
Easy movement → R01 × 5 → R03 × 5 → visualize 3 at-bats with a plan

language.say: Good effort — next one, see the ball a little longer.
language.avoid: What are you doing? / You always do that.

language.say: Let's take a breath and do one easy swing.
Great decision — that was a ball.
That was solid — how did it feel?
What was the most fun part today?
language.avoid: We're not stopping until you hit 10 good ones.

limitations: Drill categories (tee, toss, live, open/closed starting stances, high/low tee, rotational progressions) reflect common coaching practice. Specific scoring rules, round sizes, and pairings are coaching adaptations, not validated prescriptions.
Medicine-ball work supports rotational power; it does not directly fix casting, hand drop, or bat-to-ball timing.
The dashboard is a coaching record — not a diagnostic tool, readiness clearance, or comparison to age norms.
The VBA macro was written for desktop Excel but has not been run in Excel by the author; test on a copy first.
